newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aid group little affected by French truck strike.
newsitem.headline: Aid group little affected by French truck strike.

text.p: Humanitarian aid organisation, Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF), which has its logistics hub at Bordeaux airport, said it had not been seriously affected by road blocks set up in the region by striking lorry drivers over the past five days.
The lorry drivers are demanding wage hikes, shorter working hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.
Drivers union representatives and road haulage bosses were to renew talks later this afternoon aimed at settling the dispute.
The Bordeaux area had been particularly hit by the drivers action while at national level, barricades had been set up at motorways in and out of 30 towns and cities.

"There have been delays in aid supplies arriving at our Bordeaux airport hub because of the road blocks but we are more or less coping with the situation. We have a stock of supplies on site and there is also the option of transporting shipments in the bellyholds of aircraft operating scheduled passenger services to Bordeaux if necessary," an MSF official told Reuters.

Earlier this week, MSF chartered two freighter flights, using an Antonov 124 and an Ilyushin 76 from Bordeaux to the Rwandan capital of Kigali carrying a total of 135 tonnes of aid and there was a possibility of further aid flights to the same region in the next few days, the official said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
